chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Barqi, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from al-Sakuni, from Ja'far, from his father, from his ancestors, from Ali (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The camel (dhabh) may be ridden if it is pledged (as security), and upon the one who rides it is the burden of its maintenance (nafaqah). And the donkey (dar) may be drunk from (for its milk) if it is pledged, and upon the one who drinks from it is the burden of its maintenance.'

key_terms.الظَّهْرُ: The camel (specifically referring to its back for riding)
key_terms.مَرْهُوناً: Pledged or given as security for a debt

ai.seo_question: Who bears the maintenance costs for a pledged animal in Islamic jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* within the chapter on Pledges (*Al-Ruhun*), this hadith from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq clarifies that the usufruct of a pledged animal belongs to the user, who consequently bears its maintenance costs (*nafaqah*). This ruling prevents unjust enrichment by the owner while ensuring the pledged asset remains viable, reflecting the Shia juristic principle that benefits and burdens of a pledge are shared equitably between the pledgor and pledgee.
